passages.text: Then the man brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and I saw water flowing from under the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east). The water was coming down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
passages.sermon:
A man led me back to the entrance of the temple.
I saw water flowing out from under the threshold of the temple.
The water flowed toward the east.
The temple faced east.
The water came down from under the right side of the temple.
This was the south side of the temple.
The water flowed south of the altar.
passages.original: וַיְשִׁבֵנִי֮ אֶל־ פֶּ֣תַח הַבַּיִת֒ וְהִנֵּה־ מַ֣יִם יֹצְאִ֗ים מִתַּ֨חַת מִפְתַּ֤ן הַבַּ֙יִת֙ קָדִ֔ימָה כִּֽי־ פְנֵ֥י הַבַּ֖יִת קָדִ֑ים וְהַמַּ֣יִם יֹרְדִ֗ים מִתַּ֜חַת מִכֶּ֤תֶף הַבַּ֙יִת֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית מִנֶּ֖גֶב לַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: Next he brought me out through the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east, and there I saw the water trickling out from the south side.
passages.sermon:
A man guided me.
He brought me out through the north gate of the temple.
He led me around the outside of the temple.
He took me to the outer gate that faces east.
I saw water there.
The water was trickling out from the south side of the temple.
passages.original: וַיּוֹצִאֵנִי֮ דֶּֽרֶךְ־ שַׁ֣עַר צָפוֹנָה֒ וַיְסִבֵּ֙נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ ח֔וּץ אֶל־ שַׁ֣עַר הַח֔וּץ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֑ים וְהִנֵּה־ מַ֣יִם מְפַכִּ֔ים מִן־ הַכָּתֵ֖ף הַיְמָנִֽית׃

passages.text: As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through ankle-deep water.
passages.sermon:
A man stood before me.
He held a measuring line in his hand.
He walked toward the east.
He measured a distance of one thousand cubits.
He led me forward.
We walked through water.
The water reached only to my ankles.
passages.original: בְּצֵאת־ הָאִ֥ישׁ קָדִ֖ים וְקָ֣ו בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיָּ֤מָד אֶ֙לֶף֙ בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם מֵ֥י אָפְסָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Then he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through knee-deep water. Again he measured a thousand cubits and led me through waist-deep water.
passages.sermon:
A man led me.
He held a measuring line in his hand.
He measured a distance of one thousand cubits.
He led me through water that reached my knees.
He measured another one thousand cubits.
He led me through water that reached my waist.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי בַמַּ֖יִם מַ֣יִם בִּרְכָּ֑יִם וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖נִי מֵ֥י מָתְנָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Once again he measured off a thousand cubits, but now it was a river that I could not cross, because the water had risen and was deep enough for swimming—a river that could not be crossed on foot.
passages.sermon:
A man led me eastward.
He held a measuring line in his hand.
He measured a distance of one thousand cubits.
He led me to a river.
I could not cross this river.
The water had risen very high.
The water was deep enough for swimming.
No one could cross this river on foot.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣מָד אֶ֔לֶף נַ֕חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ אוּכַ֖ל לַעֲבֹ֑ר כִּֽי־ גָא֤וּ הַמַּ֙יִם֙ מֵ֣י שָׂ֔חוּ נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יֵעָבֵֽר׃

passages.text: “Son of man, do you see this?” he asked. Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to me.
He called me "son of man."
He asked me a question.
He said, "Do you see this?"
He led me.
He brought me back.
He took me to the bank of the river.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלַ֖י הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־ אָדָ֑ם וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי שְׂפַ֥ת הַנָּֽחַל׃

passages.text: When I arrived, I saw a great number of trees along both banks of the river.
passages.sermon:
Ezekiel is a prophet.
He returned to the riverbank.
He looked at the riverbank.
He saw many trees.
The trees stood on both sides of the river.
passages.original: בְּשׁוּבֵ֕נִי וְהִנֵּה֙ אֶל־ שְׂפַ֣ת הַנַּ֔חַל עֵ֖ץ רַ֣ב מְאֹ֑ד מִזֶּ֖ה וּמִזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And he said to me, “This water flows out to the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah. When it empties into the Sea, the water there becomes fresh.
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to me.
He said, “This water flows out to the eastern region.
The water goes down into the Arabah.
The water enters the Sea.
The water in the Sea becomes fresh.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּ֤יִם הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ יוֹצְאִ֗ים אֶל־ הַגְּלִילָה֙ הַקַּדְמוֹנָ֔ה וְיָרְד֖וּ עַל־ הָֽעֲרָבָ֑ה וּבָ֣אוּ הַיָּ֔מָּה אֶל־ הַיָּ֥מָּה הַמּֽוּצָאִ֖ים וְנִרְפְּאוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: Wherever the river flows, there will be swarms of living creatures and a great number of fish, because it flows there and makes the waters fresh; so wherever the river flows, everything will flourish.
passages.sermon:
The river flows from the sanctuary.
Wherever this river goes, it brings life.
Many living creatures will swarm wherever the river flows.
There will be a great number of fish in these waters.
The water from the river makes the waters fresh.
Everything that the river touches will live.
Wherever the river flows, everything will flourish.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה כָל־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֣ה׀ אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ יִשְׁרֹ֡ץ אֶ֣ל כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר֩ יָב֨וֹא שָׁ֤ם נַחֲלַ֙יִם֙ יִֽחְיֶ֔ה וְהָיָ֥ה הַדָּגָ֖ה רַבָּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד כִּי֩ בָ֨אוּ שָׁ֜מָּה הַמַּ֣יִם הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְיֵרָֽפְאוּ֙ וָחָ֔י כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יָ֥בוֹא שָׁ֖מָּה הַנָּֽחַל׃

passages.text: Fishermen will stand by the shore; from En-gedi to En-eglaim they will spread their nets to catch fish of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea.
passages.sermon:
Fishermen will stand by the shore of the river.
They will stand from En-gedi to En-eglaim.
They will spread their nets there.
They will catch many kinds of fish.
The fish will be as plentiful as the fish of the Great Sea.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֩ יַעַמְדוּ עָלָ֜יו דַּוָּגִ֗ים מֵעֵ֥ין גֶּ֙דִי֙ וְעַד־ עֵ֣ין עֶגְלַ֔יִם מִשְׁט֥וֹחַ לַֽחֲרָמִ֖ים יִהְי֑וּ לְמִינָה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה דְגָתָ֔ם כִּדְגַ֛ת הַיָּ֥ם הַגָּד֖וֹל רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: But the swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt.
passages.sermon: The swamps will not become fresh.\r\nThe marshes will not become fresh.\r\nPeople will leave them for salt.
passages.original: בִּצֹּאתוֹ וּגְבָאָ֛יו וְלֹ֥א יֵרָפְא֖וּ לְמֶ֥לַח נִתָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Along both banks of the river, fruit trees of all kinds will grow. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail. Each month they will bear fruit, because the water from the sanctuary flows to them. Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing.”
passages.sermon:
God showed Ezekiel a vision.
In this vision, a river flows from the sanctuary.
Fruit trees of every kind grow on both sides of this river.
These trees stand along the banks.
Their leaves do not wither.
Their fruit does not fail.
Every month, these trees produce new fruit.
The water from the sanctuary feeds these trees.
People use the fruit for food.
People use the leaves for healing.
passages.original: וְעַל־ הַנַּ֣חַל יַעֲלֶ֣ה עַל־ שְׂפָת֣וֹ מִזֶּ֣ה׀ וּמִזֶּ֣ה׀ כָּל־ עֵֽץ־ מַ֠אֲכָל לֹא־ יִבּ֨וֹל עָלֵ֜הוּ וְלֹֽא־ יִתֹּ֣ם פִּרְי֗וֹ לָֽחֳדָשָׁיו֙ יְבַכֵּ֔ר כִּ֣י מֵימָ֔יו מִן־ הַמִּקְדָּ֖שׁ הֵ֣מָּה יֽוֹצְאִ֑ים וְהָיוּ פִרְיוֹ֙ לְמַֽאֲכָ֔ל וְעָלֵ֖הוּ לִתְרוּפָֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the Lord GOD says: “These are the boundaries by which you are to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel; Joseph shall receive two portions.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He gives a command.
He says, “These are the boundaries of the land.
You must divide this land as an inheritance.
You must give it to the twelve tribes of Israel.
Joseph will receive two portions.”
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה גֵּ֤ה גְבוּל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתְנַחֲל֣וּ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ לִשְׁנֵ֥י עָשָׂ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יוֹסֵ֖ף חֲבָלִֽים׃

passages.text: You are to divide it equally among them. Because I swore with an uplifted hand to give it to your forefathers, this land will fall to you as an inheritance.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God told them to divide the land equally among themselves.
Each person must receive a share like his brother.
God had promised to give this land to their ancestors.
God swore with an uplifted hand to give it to them.
Now this land will belong to them as an inheritance.
passages.original: וּנְחַלְתֶּ֤ם אוֹתָהּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ כְּאָחִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֙אתִי֙ אֶת־ יָדִ֔י לְתִתָּ֖הּ לַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְנָ֨פְלָ֜ה הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לָכֶ֖ם בְּנַחֲלָֽה׃

passages.text: This shall be the boundary of the land: On the north side it will extend from the Great Sea by way of Hethlon through Lebo-hamath to Zedad, Berothah, and Sibraim (which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath), as far as Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God described the boundary of the land.
This boundary is on the north side.
The boundary begins at the Great Sea.
It goes by way of Hethlon.
It passes through Lebo-hamath.
It reaches Zedad.
It continues to Berothah.
It goes to Sibraim.
Sibraim is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath.
The boundary goes as far as Hazer-hatticon.
Hazer-hatticon is on the border of Hauran.
passages.original: וְזֶ֖ה גְּב֣וּל הָאָ֑רֶץ לִפְאַ֨ת צָפ֜וֹנָה מִן־ הַיָּ֧ם הַגָּד֛וֹל הַדֶּ֥רֶךְ חֶתְלֹ֖ן לְב֥וֹא צְדָֽדָה׃ חֲמָ֤ת׀ בֵּר֙וֹתָה֙ סִבְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר֙ בֵּין־ גְּב֣וּל דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וּבֵ֖ין גְּב֣וּל חֲמָ֑ת חָצֵר֙ הַתִּיכ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל־ גְּב֥וּל חַוְרָֽן׃

passages.text: So the border will run from the Sea to Hazar-enan, along the northern border of Damascus, with the territory of Hamath to the north. This will be the northern boundary.
passages.sermon:
God gave the people of Israel the land as an inheritance.
God set clear boundaries for this land.
The northern boundary begins at the Sea.
The border runs from the Sea to Hazar-enan.
The border follows the northern edge of Damascus.
The border includes the territory of Hamath to the north.
This line marks the northern boundary of the land.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה גְב֜וּל מִן־ הַיָּ֗ם חֲצַ֤ר עֵינוֹן֙ גְּב֣וּל דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וְצָפ֥וֹן׀ צָפ֖וֹנָה וּגְב֣וּל חֲמָ֑ת וְאֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת צָפֽוֹן׃

passages.text: On the east side the border will run between Hauran and Damascus, along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel, to the Eastern Sea and as far as Tamar. This will be the eastern boundary.
passages.sermon:
The Lord describes the boundary of the land for Israel.
The eastern boundary is on the east side.
The border runs between Hauran and Damascus.
The border also runs between Gilead and the land of Israel.
The border follows the Jordan River.
The border goes to the Eastern Sea.
The border reaches as far as Tamar.
This is the eastern boundary.
passages.original: וּפְאַ֣ת קָדִ֡ים מִבֵּ֣ין חַוְרָ֣ן וּמִבֵּין־ דַּמֶּשֶׂק֩ וּמִבֵּ֨ין הַגִּלְעָ֜ד וּמִבֵּ֨ין אֶ֤רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן מִגְּב֛וּל עַל־ הַיָּ֥ם הַקַּדְמוֹנִ֖י תָּמֹ֑דּוּ וְאֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת קָדִֽימָה׃

passages.text: On the south side it will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea. This will be the southern boundary.
passages.sermon:
The southern boundary marks the edge of the land for the people of Israel.
This boundary begins at Tamar.
It goes to the waters of Meribath-kadesh.
It follows the Brook of Egypt.
It ends at the Great Sea.
This is the southern border.
passages.original: וּפְאַת֙ נֶ֣גֶב תֵּימָ֔נָה מִתָּמָ֗ר עַד־ מֵי֙ מְרִיב֣וֹת קָדֵ֔שׁ נַחֲלָ֖ה אֶל־ הַיָּ֣ם הַגָּד֑וֹל וְאֵ֥ת פְּאַת־ תֵּימָ֖נָה נֶֽגְבָּה׃

passages.text: And on the west side, the Great Sea will be the boundary up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This will be the western boundary.
passages.sermon:
The west side is the western boundary.
The Great Sea forms this boundary.
The boundary runs from the border up to a point opposite Lebo-hamath.
This is the western boundary.
passages.original: וּפְאַת־ יָם֙ הַיָּ֣ם הַגָּד֔וֹל מִגְּב֕וּל עַד־ נֹ֖כַח לְב֣וֹא חֲמָ֑ת זֹ֖את פְּאַת־ יָֽם׃

passages.text: You are to divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
He gave them a command.
He told them to divide the land.
They must share the land among themselves.
Each tribe of Israel will receive a portion.
passages.original: וְחִלַּקְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־ הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את לָכֶ֖ם לְשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners who dwell among you and who have children. You are to treat them as native-born Israelites; along with you, they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God commanded them to divide the land as an inheritance.
They must give land to themselves.
They must also give land to the foreigners living among them.
These foreigners live among the Israelites.
These foreigners have children among the Israelites.
The Israelites must treat these foreigners as native-born Israelites.
The foreigners will receive an inheritance with the Israelites.
The foreigners will receive their share among the tribes of Israel.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה תַּפִּ֣לוּ אוֹתָהּ֮ בְּנַחֲלָה֒ לָכֶ֗ם וּלְהַגֵּרִים֙ הַגָּרִ֣ים בְּתוֹכְכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹלִ֥דוּ בָנִ֖ים בְּתֽוֹכְכֶ֑ם וְהָי֣וּ לָכֶ֗ם כְּאֶזְרָח֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִתְּכֶם֙ יִפְּל֣וּ בְנַחֲלָ֔ה בְּת֖וֹךְ שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: In whatever tribe a foreigner dwells, you are to assign his inheritance there,” declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He gives a command.
A foreigner may live among you.
He may dwell in a tribe of Israel.
You must give the foreigner his inheritance in that tribe.
You must assign it there.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה בַשֵּׁ֔בֶט אֲשֶׁר־ גָּ֥ר הַגֵּ֖ר אִתּ֑וֹ שָׁ֚ם תִּתְּנ֣וּ נַחֲלָת֔וֹ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
